profile.reading:
STACK Infrastructure's SVY02 campus sits in Santa Clara, California, part of the Silicon Valley market alongside the company's larger San Jose campus, SVY01. SVY02 is a single-building, 9-acre site, building SVY02A, totaling 560,440 square feet and 48 megawatts of IT capacity, and STACK's own page states it has a dedicated onsite electrical substation, a common feature at large-scale data center conversions that require substantial dedicated power delivery. Notably, STACK's own marketing states that this site was formerly the headquarters of Memorex, the well-known 20th-century technology company associated with magnetic recording tape and data storage media, giving this record a specific, checkable historical anchor even though the exact current street address could not be independently confirmed this session. STACK describes the location as minutes from San Jose International Airport. STACK, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, operates roughly 8.5 gigawatts of capacity built or under development across 24 global markets company-wide, and describes its overall Silicon Valley market as "3 campuses across 97 acres" totaling 150 megawatts, though only SVY01 (100MW) and SVY02 (48MW) are individually named and detailed on STACK's site, together totaling 148 megawatts, a small unreconciled gap suggesting an undisclosed or unannounced third campus, noted honestly rather than resolved. No year of completion or named power utility (Santa Clara operates its own municipal electric utility, Silicon Valley Power, though this was not confirmed as SVY02's specific provider) is disclosed, and tenant identities are not publicly disclosed.

STACK has stated a company-wide net-zero greenhouse gas emissions commitment for 2050, organized under five focus areas covering carbon, energy, water, waste and circularity, and land use and biodiversity, with annual public impact reports. Santa Clara operates its own municipally owned electric utility, Silicon Valley Power, distinct from the investor-owned PG&E service territory that covers much of the rest of the South Bay, a distinction relevant to power procurement for any large site in the city even though SVY02's specific utility arrangement was not confirmed on STACK's public page.

reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's STACK SVY02 in Santa Clara County publishes floor area but not power consumption, making it impossible to assess its role in AI infrastructure without additional disclosure.

The facility occupies 560,440 square feet across a single building on a 9-acre site in what was formerly Memorex headquarters. That scale places it among the larger data centers in Silicon Valley by physical footprint. The operator's public specification page does not, however, disclose megawatts of IT capacity, power density, or cooling architecture. Floor area alone cannot be translated into compute density or workload type without knowing how intensively the space is provisioned.

This gap matters because power is the limiting constraint on AI scaling. A facility of this size could support anywhere from modest colocation to high-density accelerator deployment depending on electrical and cooling infrastructure. Without that information, the site cannot be ranked against other California facilities or assessed for its contribution to regional AI infrastructure capacity.

California hosts 103 mapped facilities in this data set, of which only five have published power figures totaling 170 MW. STACK SVY02 is counted in the facility inventory but cannot be included in any power-based analysis. Its location in Santa Clara County places it at the center of the densest AI infrastructure cluster in the country, but public data does not yet reveal what its actual computational role is.
